'''Isaac Jones''' (born July 11, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Detroit Pistons]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Motor City Cruise]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Wenatchee Valley College|Wenatchee Valley Knights]], [[Idaho Vandals men's basketball|Idaho Vandals]] and [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State Cougars]]. Jones signed a two-way contract with the [[Sacramento Kings]] after going undrafted in the [[2024 NBA Draft]].

==Early life and high school career==
Jones grew up in [[Spanaway, Washington]] and attended [[Orting High School]]. He entered high school at 5' 5" and had grown to 6' 4" by his senior year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/washington-state/article/wsu-mens-basketball-isaac-jones-from-tiny-teen-to-college-beast-222742184/|title=From tiny teen to college beast: The wild journey of WSU's Isaac Jones|first=Jamey|last=Vinnick|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=December 12, 2023|access-date=May 14, 2024}}</ref>

==College career==
Jones did not initially attend college after graduating high school and worked at the loading dock at a pipe manufacturing company. He grew another five inches.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/march-madness-washington-state-5957c0fe50d8ca14195272f14ab8ee61|title=Isaac Jones once loaded trucks. Now the Washington State star plays for Sweet 16 spot|first=Eric|last=Olson|website=[[APNews.com]]|date=March 22, 2024|access-date=May 14, 2024}}</ref> A year later, Jones enrolled at [[Wenatchee Valley College]] at the urging of a former high school teammate, who was told he could play for the basketball team if he could also find another player who was at least 6' 8".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wenatcheeworld.com/sports/isaac-jones-remarkable-journey-from-walk-on-to-nwac-leading-scorer/article_852f6308-9f07-11ec-8ce2-1f75dd4dad3b.html|title=Isaac Jones' remarkable journey from walk-on to NWAC-leading scorer|work=[[Wenatchee World]]|date=March 9, 2022|access-date=May 14, 2024}}</ref> In his final season with the Knights, he was named the [[Northwest Athletic Conference]] Player of the Year after averaging 25.3 points and 13.2 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2024/mar/20/dave-boling-hard-working-isaac-jones-has-gone-from/|title=Dave Boling: Hard-working Isaac Jones has gone from pipe-supply company to supplying WSU with an inside presence ahead of NCAA Tournament opener|first=Dave|last=Boling|work=[[The Spokesman-Review]]|date=March 20, 2024|access-date=May 17, 2024}}</ref>

After three years at Wenatchee Valley College, Jones transferred to [[Idaho Vandals men's basketball|Idaho]].<ref>{{cite web |date=June 1, 2022 |title=Vandals sign prolific JC forward Isaac Jones after he spurns Power 5 teams |url=https://dnews.com/sports/vandals-sign-prolific-jc-forward-isaac-jones-after-he-spurns-power-5-teams/article_52c88eeb-8d7a-5f32-b95a-ce8ef1112d0e.html |url-access=limited |access-date=May 15, 2024 |work=[[Moscow-Pullman Daily News]]}}</ref> He was named the [[Big Sky Conference]] Newcomer of the Year and second-team All-Big Sky after averaging 19.4 points and 7.8 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web |last=Wiebe |first=Stephan |date=March 9, 2024 |title=WASHINGTON STATE MEN'S BASKETBALL: Hoops success wasn't always part of life for Wazzu star Isaac Jones |url=https://www.lmtribune.com/sports/washington-state-mens-basketball-hoops-success-wasn-t-always-part-of-life-for-wazzu-star/article_0fa78499-7bd8-5620-955a-f8394b81a72f.html |access-date=May 15, 2024 |work=[[Lewiston Morning Tribune]] |archive-date=May 15, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240515135325/https://www.lmtribune.com/sports/washington-state-mens-basketball-hoops-success-wasn-t-always-part-of-life-for-wazzu-star/article_0fa78499-7bd8-5620-955a-f8394b81a72f.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Following the end of the season, Jones entered the NCAA transfer portal.<ref>{{cite web |last=Pixley |first=Trevan |date=April 27, 2023 |title=Transfer portal continues to haunt Vandals |url=https://dnews.com/sports/transfer-portal-continues-to-haunt-vandals/article_af59331a-ec5e-5e03-b47f-7dce2ebffc7e.html |access-date=May 15, 2024 |work=[[Moscow-Pullman Daily News]]}}</ref>

Jones ultimately transferred to [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Clark |first=Colton |date=May 12, 2023 |title=Isaac Jones, a star forward for Idaho last season, transfers to Washington State |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2023/may/12/isaac-jones-a-star-forward-for-idaho-last-season-t/ |access-date=May 15, 2024 |work=[[The Spokesman-Review]]}}</ref> He averaged 15.3 points and 7.6 rebounds per game and was named first-team All-[[Pac-12 Conference]].<ref>{{cite web |date=April 2, 2024 |title=Locally: Washington State standout Isaac Jones to compete at prestigious Portsmouth Invitational Tournament |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2024/apr/02/locally-washington-state-standout-isaac-jones-to-c/ |access-date=May 15, 2024 |work=[[The Spokesman-Review]]}}</ref>

==Professional career==
After going undrafted in the [[2024 NBA draft]], Jones signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Sacramento Kings]] on July 3, 2024.<ref>{{cite web|first=Rory|last=Maher|title=Kings Sign Isaiah Crawford, Isaac Jones To Two-Way Deals|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/07/kings-to-sign-isaiah-crawford-isaac-jones-to-two-way-deals.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=July 3, 2024|access-date=July 3, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=July 3, 2024 |title=Sacramento Kings Sign Isaiah Crawford and Isaac Jones to Two-Way Contracts |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/sacramento-kings-sign-isaiah-crawford-and-isaac-jones-to-two-way-contracts |access-date=July 3, 2024 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>
On March 22, 2025, Jones got converted from a [[two-way contract]] to a standard NBA contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kings Convert Isaac Jones to Standard NBA Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-convert-isaac-jones-to-standard-nba-contract|date=March 22, 2025|website=NBA.com|access-date=March 22, 2025}}</ref> He made 40 appearances for the Kings during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 3.4 points, 1.4 rebounds and 0.3 assists.

Jones played in three games, including one start, for Sacramento during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], averaging one point, 0.7 rebounds and 0.3 assists. On November 4, 2025, Jones was waived by the Kings following the signing of [[Precious Achiuwa]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sacramento Kings waiving fan favorite to sign NBA veteran free agent|url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/nba/sacramento-kings/article312772154.html|access-date=November 6, 2025|website=sacbee.com|language=en|date=November 4, 2025|last=Anderson|first=Jason}}</ref>

On November 6, 2025, Jones was claimed off waivers by the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Nunes | first=Brenden | title=Pistons claim former King F/C Isaac Jones off waivers | website=Sactown Sports | date=2025-11-06 | url=https://sactownsports.com/59816/pistons-claim-isaac-jones-waivers/ | access-date=2025-12-05}}</ref> Jones was waived by the Pistons on February 4, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Isaac Jones: Let go by Detroit|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/isaac-jones-let-go-by-detroit/|access-date=February 10, 2026|website=oursportscentral.com|language=en|date=February 4, 2026}}</ref> However, on February 10, Detroit re-signed Jones to a two-way contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pistons' Isaac Jones: Signed by Detroit|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pistons-isaac-jones-signed-by-detroit/|access-date=February 10, 2026|website=oursportscentral.com|language=en|date=February 10, 2026}}</ref>
